question: Should OpenClaw publish Gateway client-generation support as a versioned OpenAPI/Swagger document, a static or served TypeBox/JSON Schema contract, or keep the current Gateway protocol docs as the supported surface?
rationale: This choice defines an external API contract for Gateway methods, auth, endpoint visibility, versioning, and plugin behavior, so automation should not choose the contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Static Artifact
options.body: Publish a release-attached or generated static schema for client generation without adding a runtime endpoint yet.

options.title: Defer To Existing Protocol Docs
options.body: Close later only if maintainers decide the TypeBox/JSON Schema pipeline and Gateway protocol docs are the intended client-generation surface.

recommendation.title: Design Public Schema Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this open while maintainers choose the schema format, exposure path, versioning model, and security boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway protocol and method descriptor work makes this the strongest current-main routing signal for the public API boundary decision.
